- mw-cp: Mike Wright's Checkpoint Process — pre-commit checks, doc updates, detailed commit, and push
- claude-mem:do: Execute a plan using subagents for implementation
- claude-mem:make-plan: Create an implementation plan with documentation discovery
- claude-mem:mem-search: Search claude-mem's persistent cross-session memory database. Use when user asks "did we already solve this?", "how did we do X last time?", or needs work from previous sessions.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request

1	//! Built-in function registry and dispatch for MLPL.
2	//!
3	//! Saga 32 step 002: `error` + `prng` extracted into
4	//! `mlpl-runtime-core`; the t-SNE + PCA family extracted into

17	pub use builtins::call_builtin;
18	pub use llm_builtins::call_ollama;
19	pub use mlpl_runtime_core::RuntimeError;

21	/// Iterate every builtin name dispatched by [`call_builtin`].
22	/// Aggregates the per-module `NAMES` constants plus
23	/// [`builtins::LOCAL_NAMES`]. Used by the help-completeness
24	/// test in `mlpl-eval/tests/help_completeness_tests.rs` to
25	/// catch undocumented runtime builtins.
26	pub fn runtime_builtin_names() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> {
27	    builtins::LOCAL_NAMES
28	        .iter()
29	        .chain(math_builtins::NAMES)
30	        .chain(conv_builtins::NAMES)
31	        .chain(rnn_builtins::NAMES)
32	        .chain(random_builtins::NAMES)
33	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_data::dataset_builtins::NAMES)
34	        .chain(ml_builtins::NAMES)
35	        .chain(ensemble_builtins::NAMES)
36	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_data::embedding_builtins::NAMES)
37	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_dim_reduction::tsne_builtin::NAMES)
38	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_dim_reduction::pca_builtin::NAMES)
39	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_umap::umap_graph::NAMES)
40	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_umap::umap_builtin::NAMES)
41	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_mds_rp::mds::NAMES)
42	        .chain(mlpl_runtime_mds_rp::random_projection::NAMES)
43	        .copied()

Components are top-level, NOT counted in sw-checklist, and are each multi-crate workspaces.

Dependency hierarchy (higher depends on lower):
- **Paths** (top) -> Tutorials -> Demos -> base

There should be a `tutorials` component and a `paths` component, each with separate crates for grouping modules per concept.

**Why:** The current monorepo has all content in one workspace. Leveled dependencies enforce that higher-level content (paths) can reference lower-level content (tutorials, demos) but not vice versa. Each component being its own workspace also helps with disk-constrained builds (separate `target/` dirs).

**How to apply:** When planning new content organization or refactoring content crates, structure as independent component workspaces with strict leveled dependencies. Don't put tutorials and paths in the same crate hierarchy as base demos.

3	use mlpl_core::Span;

5	/// The kind of a lexer token.
6	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
7	pub enum TokenKind {
8	    /// Integer literal.
9	    IntLit(i64),
10	    /// Float literal.
11	    FloatLit(f64),
12	    /// Identifier.
13	    Ident(String),
14	    /// Builtin / operator reference: `:foo`, `:+`, `:max`, `:*`.
15	    /// The lexer produces this whenever a `:` is immediately
16	    /// followed (no intervening space) by an identifier-start
17	    /// character or one of `+ * / -`. The annotation colon
18	    /// (`x : [batch] = ...`) keeps producing `Colon` because
19	    /// it requires a space after the `:`, then a `[`. This
20	    /// is the canonical way to pass a function / operator
21	    /// reference to a higher-order builtin like `reduce` or
22	    /// `map`. See `docs/glossary.md` "Reduce".
23	    BuiltinRef(String),
24	    /// String literal (double-quoted, escapes processed).
25	    StrLit(String),
26	    /// `(`
27	    LParen,
28	    /// `)`
29	    RParen,
30	    /// `[`
31	    LBracket,
32	    /// `]`
33	    RBracket,
34	    /// `,`
35	    Comma,
36	    /// `=`
37	    Equals,
38	    /// `:` (axis-label annotation, Saga 11.5 Phase 2).
39	    Colon,
40	    /// `;`
41	    Semicolon,
42	    /// `+`
43	    Plus,
44	    /// `-`
45	    Minus,
46	    /// `*`
47	    Star,
48	    /// `/`
49	    Slash,
50	    /// `{`
51	    LBrace,
52	    /// `}`
53	    RBrace,
54	    /// `.` (field access on records, Saga 29 step 001). Distinct
55	    /// from float-literal decimal points -- floats lex via
56	    /// `lex_number` which only consumes `digit.digit`; a bare `.`
57	    /// at the lexer fall-through is this token.
58	    Dot,
59	    /// `repeat` keyword.
60	    Repeat,
61	    /// `train` keyword.
62	    Train,
63	    /// `for` keyword (streaming-iter, Saga 12 step 003).
64	    For,
65	    /// `in` keyword (only meaningful inside `for ... in ...`).
66	    In,
67	    /// `experiment` keyword (Saga 12 step 007).
68	    Experiment,
69	    /// `device` keyword (Saga 14 step 004). Introduces a scoped
70	    /// `device("mlx") { body }` or `device("cpu") { body }` block
71	    /// that dispatches ops inside the body through the named
72	    /// runtime target.
73	    Device,
74	    /// `if` keyword (Saga 31 step 004). Introduces an `if cond
75	    /// { then } else { else }` expression that returns the value
76	    /// of whichever branch was taken. `else` is required.
77	    If,
78	    /// `else` keyword (Saga 31 step 004). Always paired with `if`.
79	    Else,
80	    /// `while` keyword (Saga 31 step 005). Introduces a `while cond
81	    /// { body }` loop. Exits when `cond` is falsy or `break` fires.
82	    While,
83	    /// `break` keyword (Saga 31 step 005). Exits the nearest
84	    /// enclosing `while` loop. Optionally followed by a value.
85	    Break,
86	    /// `continue` keyword (Saga 31 step 005). Skips the rest of
87	    /// the current `while` iteration; cond is re-checked.
88	    Continue,
89	    /// `def` keyword (Saga 46). Introduces a user-defined function.
90	    Def,
91	    /// `return` keyword (Saga 46). Early exit from a UDF body.
92	    Return,
93	    /// Newline (statement separator).
94	    Newline,
95	    /// End of input.
96	    Eof,
97	}

102	    /// What kind of token.

content.content:
Insert a new pending step at a chosen position, shifting later steps up

Use when a bug or unplanned task needs to slot in before existing pending work. The new step lands at position `after + 1`; every pending/in-progress step with a number greater than `after` shifts up by one (step.toml `number` and the on-disk `NNN-slug` directory name are both updated). The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

Usage: agentrail insert [OPTIONS] --after <AFTER> --slug <SLUG> --prompt <PROMPT>

Options:
      --after <AFTER>
          Position to insert after (0 prepends). The new step becomes N+1

      --slug <SLUG>
          Slug for the new step

          Step prompt: text, file path, or "-" for stdin

          Step role (production, deterministic, validation, meta)

pub fn try_call(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Option<Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError>> {
    match name {
        "iota" | "range" => Some(crate::compute::iota(name, args)),
        "shape" => Some(crate::shape::shape(name, args)),
        "rank" => Some(crate::shape::rank(name, args)),
        "reshape" => Some(crate::shape::reshape(name, args)),
        "transpose" => Some(crate::shape::transpose(name, args)),
        "reduce_add" | "reduce_mul" => Some(crate::reduce::reduce(name, args)),
        "argmax" => Some(crate::reduce::argmax(name, args)),
        "dot" => Some(crate::compute::dot(name, args)),
        "matmul" => Some(crate::compute::matmul(name, args)),
        "patchify" => Some(crate::slice::patchify(name, args)),
        "concat" if args.len() == 3 => Some(crate::slice::concat(name, args)),
        "take" => Some(crate::slice::take(name, args)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

content.text:
Good question. Let me address the strategy and then start the extraction.

## Strategy Analysis: Where to attack first?

**Worst-offenders first wins.** Here's why:

**Top (components):** Currently only 1 component exists (`mlpl-session`). Components are unbounded — no FAILs at this level. Working here is pure infrastructure setup with delayed payoff.

**Middle (crates with too many modules):** This is where the worst offenders live:
- `mlpl-eval` (96 modules, 14× over budget)
- `mlpl-web` (75 modules, 11× over budget)
- `mlpl-array` (13 modules), `mlpl-viz` (13 modules)

**Bottom (modules with too many fns):** Often blocked by middle. Can't split a module if the crate is already at module-count FAIL — you'd just trade one FAIL for another.

**The dependency chain:** splitting a function needs module room → splitting a module needs crate room → splitting a crate needs component room. When `mlpl-eval` has 96 modules (FAIL), any internal cleanup is wasted motion until the crate is decomposed.

**Right order:**
1. **Worst middle offenders first** (mlpl-eval, mlpl-web) — they're so far over budget that they block everything downstream and consume warning budgets unfairly.
2. **In parallel: continue extracting from at-capacity crates** like mlpl-runtime (where we have proven patterns).
3. **Components only when** a logical grouping spans crates that should level (e.g., paths > tutorials > demos).
4. **Bottom-up cleanup last** — after the structural FAILs are gone.

What I've been doing on mlpl-runtime is the right pattern *for that crate*. But the leverage point for the whole codebase is **mlpl-eval and mlpl-web**.

Now let me set up step 004 and extract mlpl-runtime-ml.

1	//! Built-in function registry and dispatch.
2	//!
3	//! Most array/shape/reduce/slice builtins live in
4	//! `mlpl-runtime-array`; the rest are dispatched through the
5	//! `try_external_dispatchers` chain below. This module only
6	//! holds the dispatch glue plus the `grid` / `concat` (2-arg)
7	//! arms that don't fit the per-crate `try_call` pattern.
8	
9	use mlpl_array::DenseArray;
10	
11	use mlpl_runtime_core::error::RuntimeError;
12	
13	/// Names handled by the local match in `match_local_builtin`
14	/// below (i.e., names NOT covered by any per-crate `try_call`).
15	/// Currently just `grid`, which dispatches into mlpl-runtime-data.
16	pub(crate) const LOCAL_NAMES: &[&str] = &["grid"];
17	
18	/// Try every external per-module `try_call` dispatcher in
19	/// registration order; returns `Some(result)` for the first
20	/// module that recognizes `name`.
21	fn try_external_dispatchers(
22	    name: &str,
23	    args: &[DenseArray],
24	) -> Option<Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError>> {
25	    mlpl_runtime_math::try_call(name, args.to_vec())
26	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_array::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
27	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_conv::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
28	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_rnn::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
29	        .or_else(|| crate::random_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
30	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_data::dataset_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
31	        .or_else(|| crate::ml_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
32	        .or_else(|| crate::ensemble_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
33	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_data::embedding_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
34	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_dim_reduction::tsne_builtin::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
35	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_dim_reduction::pca_builtin::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
36	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_umap::umap_graph::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
37	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_umap::umap_builtin::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
38	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_mds_rp::mds::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
39	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_mds_rp::random_projection::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
40	}
41	
42	/// Dispatch a built-in function call by name.
43	pub fn call_builtin(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError> {
44	    if let Some(result) = try_external_dispatchers(name, &args) {
45	        return result;
46	    }
47	    match_local_builtin(name, args)
48	}
49	
50	/// Match the local in-crate builtin names. Currently just `grid`
51	/// (which lives in mlpl-runtime-data but isn't behind a `try_call`).
52	fn match_local_builtin(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError> {
53	    match name {
54	        "grid" => mlpl_runtime_data::grid_builtin::builtin_grid(name, args),
55	        _ => Err(RuntimeError::UnknownFunction(name.into())),
56	    }
57	}

---
name: extract-to-components
description: Extractions belong in proper components (multi-crate workspaces), not flat in the main workspace
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When extracting a logical group of crates, put them in a **component** (a top-level multi-crate workspace under `components/<name>/`), NOT flat in the main `sw-mlpl/crates/` directory.

**Each major feature should be its own component.** Many, many components. Each component has a few sparse crates; each crate has a few sparse modules; each module has a few sparse functions.

**Why:** The user has repeatedly emphasized this. Flat workspace = sprawl that fights the sw-checklist limits. Components are unbounded (not counted by sw-checklist) and provide natural decomposition boundaries. The existing `components/mlpl-session/` is the model.

**How to apply:**
- Before extracting a new crate, ask: which component does this belong in?
- If the natural component doesn't exist yet, **create it** as part of the extraction
- Don't just dump new crates into `sw-mlpl/crates/` — that's the failure mode
- When refactoring, look for groups of related crates already in `crates/` and migrate them into a new component together

**Concrete groupings to create:**
- `components/mlpl-runtime/` — runtime + all runtime-* crates (math, conv, rnn, array, ml, data, dim-reduction, umap, mds-rp, core)
- `components/mlpl-language/` — core, array, parser, lexer, macro
- `components/mlpl-eval/` — eval, eval-core, web-eval, autograd
- `components/mlpl-web/` — web app + web-lessons + web-path-body + viz
- `components/mlpl-tools/` — repl, cli, build, lab, serve, reg
- `components/mlpl-models/` — already exists as mlpl-session, expand

aiTitle: Organize workspace dependencies and crate hierarchy

content.text:
Now the plan you asked for. Below is a complete physical layout based on the dependency data I just collected.

---

# Component Restructuring Plan

## Principles

1. **Components are top-level features.** Each represents one cohesive concern of the system.
2. **Components contain sparse crates** (few crates per component); crates contain sparse modules; modules contain sparse functions.
3. **Dependencies flow downward only** — strict DAG; no cycles between components.
4. **Shared `target/`** via `.cargo/config.toml` at the repo root.
5. **No crate lives directly in `sw-mlpl/crates/`** — that directory becomes empty (or deleted) after migration.

## Dependency layers (bottom → top)

From the data I collected:

```
Layer 0 (no intra-workspace deps): mlpl-core, mlpl-eval-core, mlpl-bpe-core,
                                   mlpl-web-lessons, mlpl-web-path-body, mlpl-lab

Layer 1 (depend on Layer 0):       mlpl-array, mlpl-lexer

Layer 2:                           mlpl-parser, mlpl-loader-helpers,
                                   mlpl-runtime-core, mlpl-trace, mlpl-rt,
                                   mlpl-autograd

Layer 3:                           mlpl-runtime-{math,conv,rnn,array,ml,data,
                                                 dim-reduction,umap,mds-rp},
                                   mlpl-mlx-rt, mlpl-viz, mlpl-lower-rs,
                                   mlpl-env-traits

Layer 4:                           mlpl-runtime, mlpl-macro, mlpl-models-*,
                                   mlpl-ml

Layer 5:                           mlpl-eval, mlpl-wasm

Layer 6:                           mlpl-cli, mlpl-bench, mlpl-parity-tests,
                                   mlpl-reg, mlpl-web-eval

Layer 7:                           mlpl-serve, mlpl-build, mlpl

Layer 8 (apps):                    mlpl-repl, mlpl-web, mlpl-mlx-serve
```

## Proposed components

### `components/lang-core/` — language foundations
**Purpose:** Types and primitives every other component depends on. Pure data, no behavior.

| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-core` | spans, identifiers, base types |
| `mlpl-array` | DenseArray, Shape (pure compute substrate) |
| `mlpl-eval-core` | shared eval types (no eval logic) |

**Why grouped:** all Layer 0–1, depended on by every other component. The foundation.

---

### `components/lang-syntax/` — lexer + parser + AST
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-lexer` | tokens, lexing |
| `mlpl-parser` | AST + parser |
| `mlpl-macro` | proc macros |
| `mlpl-lower-rs` | parser → IR lowering |

**Why grouped:** the source-text-to-AST pipeline. All sit between core and any consumer that reads MLPL source.

**Depends on:** `lang-core`

---

### `components/runtime/` — built-in function runtime
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-runtime-core` | RuntimeError, prng |
| `mlpl-runtime-math` | math + constructor builtins |
| `mlpl-runtime-array` | shape/reduce/slice/linalg builtins |
| `mlpl-runtime-conv` | conv2d, pool2d |
| `mlpl-runtime-rnn` | rnn_cell, lstm_cell |
| `mlpl-runtime-ml` | softmax, one_hot, sinusoidal, cross_entropy |
| `mlpl-runtime-data` | dataset, embedding, grid builtins |
| `mlpl-runtime-dim-reduction` | t-SNE, PCA |
| `mlpl-runtime-umap` | UMAP |
| `mlpl-runtime-mds-rp` | MDS, random projection |
| `mlpl-runtime` | dispatch facade (call_builtin) |

**Why grouped:** the entire builtin function family, internally cohesive. 11 sparse crates each at 3–5 modules.

**Depends on:** `lang-core`

---

### `components/autograd/` — automatic differentiation
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-autograd` | tape, gradients, ops backward |
| `mlpl-trace` | execution trace export |

**Why grouped:** trace + autograd both observe runtime execution. Trace currently consumes autograd-shaped data structures.

**Depends on:** `lang-core`, `runtime`

---

### `components/native-rt/` — non-WASM native execution backends
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-rt` | native runtime layer |
| `mlpl-mlx-rt` | Apple MLX backend |

**Why grouped:** non-WASM backends; both bind into native compute libraries. (Future: cuda-rt, vulkan-rt.)

**Depends on:** `lang-core`

---

### `components/viz/` — visualization rendering
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-viz` | trace → SVG/JSON viz renderer |

**Single-crate today but logically distinct.** Future: scatter, heatmap, decision-boundary as sibling crates inside.

**Depends on:** `lang-core`, `autograd` (for trace)

---

### `components/models/` — ML model library
**Rename `components/mlpl-session/` to `components/models/`** (or keep the existing name — see note). Its sub-crates already follow the pattern:

| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-bpe-core` | BPE tokenizer core |
| `mlpl-env-traits` | environment capability traits |
| `mlpl-loader-helpers` | parameter loaders |
| `mlpl-models-feasibility` | feasibility checks |
| `mlpl-models-freeze` | layer freezing |
| `mlpl-models-inspect` | model introspection |
| `mlpl-models-llm` | LLM model definitions |
| `mlpl-models-mutate` | model mutation ops |
| `mlpl-models-tape` | model gradient tape |
| `mlpl-models-tune` | model tuning |

**Depends on:** `lang-core`, `lang-syntax`, `autograd`, `runtime`

*Note: I'd rename to `components/models/` for naming consistency, but happy to leave as `mlpl-session` to avoid churning a working component. **Confirm before I do the rename.***

---

### `components/eval/` — interpreter
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-eval` | tree-walking interpreter |

**Why a component despite single crate:** `mlpl-eval` has 96 modules and is the #1 sw-checklist FAIL in the codebase. Once it's in its own component, the **next saga** can decompose it into several siblings: `mlpl-eval-dispatch`, `mlpl-eval-attention`, `mlpl-eval-tokenizer`, `mlpl-eval-image-io`, `mlpl-eval-gradients`, `mlpl-eval-experiments`, etc.

**Depends on:** `lang-core`, `lang-syntax`, `autograd`, `runtime`, `models`, `viz`, `native-rt`

---

### `components/wasm/` — WASM packaging
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-wasm` | WASM-side eval glue |
| `mlpl-web-eval` | WASM eval entry points |

**Depends on:** `eval`

---

### `components/web/` — browser UI
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-web` (app) | Yew frontend |
| `mlpl-web-lessons` | lesson content |
| `mlpl-web-path-body` | path body rendering |

**Why grouped:** all live in the browser. `mlpl-web` (currently 75 modules, FAIL) will need further decomposition inside this component — the **next-next saga**: `web-completion`, `web-viz3d`, `web-upload`, `web-render`, `web-components`.

**Depends on:** `wasm`, `eval`, `lang-syntax`

---

### `components/cli/` — command-line utilities
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-cli` | CLI helpers |
| `mlpl-repl` (app) | REPL |
| `mlpl-build` (app) | build tool |
| `mlpl-lab` (app) | lab playground |
| `mlpl` | top-level CLI |

**Depends on:** `eval`, `lang-syntax`, `runtime`

---

### `components/serve/` — HTTP services
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-serve` | core HTTP server crate |
| `mlpl-mlx-serve` (currently in `services/`) | MLX-backed serve |

**Why merged:** `mlpl-mlx-serve` is currently in `services/` but logically belongs with the serve crate. Consolidate.

**Depends on:** `eval`, `lang-syntax`, `cli`, `native-rt`

---

### `components/dev-tools/` — testing / benchmarking
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-bench` | benchmarks |
| `mlpl-parity-tests` | parity test harness |
| `mlpl-reg` | regression tests |

**Why grouped:** none ship in production; all are dev/test infrastructure.

**Depends on:** `eval`, `lang-syntax`

---

### `vendor/` (unchanged)
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlx-rs` | vendored mlx-rs with packaging fix |

Stays vendored as-is.

---

├── .cargo/
│   └── config.toml              # [build] target-dir = "target"
├── target/                      # ONE shared target directory

Cargo discovers `.cargo/config.toml` by walking up from the current directory. Any `cargo` invocation from anywhere in the tree resolves the same shared `target/` at `sw-mlpl/target/`. No per-component target dirs. Disk-friendly.

## Migration plan (12 steps, one saga each)

Order matters — bottom-up so dependents always compile.

| Step | Component | Crates moved | Rationale |
|------|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| 1 | Set up `.cargo/config.toml` shared target | — | enable rest of plan |
| 2 | `lang-core` | mlpl-core, mlpl-array, mlpl-eval-core | foundation; everything depends on it |
| 3 | `lang-syntax` | mlpl-lexer, mlpl-parser, mlpl-macro, mlpl-lower-rs | next layer up |
| 4 | `runtime` | 11 runtime-* crates | clean self-contained family |
| 5 | `autograd` | mlpl-autograd, mlpl-trace | small, independent |
| 6 | `native-rt` | mlpl-rt, mlpl-mlx-rt | small, independent |
| 7 | `viz` | mlpl-viz | single-crate component |
| 8 | Rename `mlpl-session` → `models` | — | cosmetic, optional, ask first |
| 9 | `eval` | mlpl-eval | single-crate now; future decomposition next saga |
| 10 | `wasm` | mlpl-wasm, mlpl-web-eval | depends on eval |
| 11 | `cli` + `serve` | apps + mlpl-cli + mlpl-serve + mlpl-mlx-serve, mlpl, mlpl-build, mlpl-lab, mlpl-repl | top of stack |
| 12 | `web` + `dev-tools` | mlpl-web, web-lessons, web-path-body, bench, parity-tests, reg | leaf consumers |

Each step: create component, move crates with `git mv`, update path deps inside moved crates, remove from root `Cargo.toml`, verify `cargo check` from a clean state.

## Per-step recipe

1. `mkdir -p components/<name>/crates`
2. Write `components/<name>/Cargo.toml` workspace manifest
3. `git mv` each crate from `crates/<x>/` to `components/<name>/crates/<x>/`
4. Update path dependencies in moved crates: `path = "../../<other-component>/crates/<dep>"` for cross-component deps; `path = "../<dep>"` for same-component
5. Remove moved crates from root `Cargo.toml` members
6. `cargo check --workspace` (from each affected workspace root)
7. `cargo test` for affected crates
8. Commit; push

## Open questions before I start

1. **Rename `mlpl-session` → `models`?** Cosmetic but consistent. (Default: leave as-is to minimize churn.)
2. **Apps in components/cli/ and components/web/, or keep `apps/`?** I'd fold them in for consistency. Confirm.
3. **Order — start with bottom (`lang-core`) or the just-extracted `runtime` family that's freshest in my head?** I lean bottom-up but happy either way.
4. **One saga = one component, or batch multiple into one?** I'd do one saga per component for safety; you've taught me to keep diffs reviewable.

Tell me which questions to resolve and I'll start with whichever component you want first.

# Single shared target directory for the whole repo.
#
# Cargo discovers this config by walking up from the invocation
# directory. Any `cargo` command -- whether run from this main
# workspace, from a nested component workspace under components/,
# or from a service under services/ -- resolves to the same
# target/ tree at the repo root.
#
# Why: as the project decomposes into many component workspaces
# (saga 51+), each would otherwise grow its own multi-GB target/.
# A single shared target keeps disk usage bounded (~25 GB after a
# full build vs N x 25 GB) and makes cross-workspace incremental
# rebuilds cache-warm.
#
# `target-dir` is relative to this config file's directory, so it
# resolves to sw-mlpl/target/ regardless of where cargo is invoked
# from.

[build]
target-dir = "target"

cat > /tmp/saga52-plan.md <<'EOF'
# components/lang-core/ migration (saga 52)

First component-migration saga. Move the three foundational crates
(mlpl-core, mlpl-array, mlpl-eval-core) into a new
`components/lang-core/` nested workspace. Bottom of the dep stack,
so every other crate's path references must be updated.

## Why these three together

- mlpl-core: spans, identifiers, base types -- depended on by ~15
- mlpl-array: DenseArray, Shape -- depended on by ~30
- mlpl-eval-core: shared eval types -- depended on by ~7

All Layer 0-1, no intra-workspace deps among them except
mlpl-array -> mlpl-core. Move them together so referrers update
once, not three times.

## Step plan

1. **scaffold-component**: create `components/lang-core/Cargo.toml`
   (workspace manifest), `components/lang-core/crates/` empty
   directory. Verify the empty component workspace builds.
2. **move-mlpl-core**: `git mv crates/mlpl-core
   components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-core`. Update root Cargo.toml
   members. Update every Cargo.toml that has
   `mlpl-core = { path = "../mlpl-core" }` to point to the new
   location. Verify full workspace build.
3. **move-mlpl-array**: `git mv` then update all referrers (the
   biggest batch -- ~30 crates).
4. **move-mlpl-eval-core**: `git mv` then update all referrers
   (~7 crates).
5. **close**: language-status update, --done.

Each step ends with a green `cargo check --workspace` and pushed
commits, so no step leaves the tree broken.

## Path-reference rules

---
name: no-git-add-all
description: Never use `git add -A` or `git add .` — always stage specific files; bulk-staging sweeps in untracked scratch
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Never use `git add -A` or `git add .` in this repo. Always stage specific files by name or directory.

**Why:** The repo's working tree often has untracked files that should NOT be committed:
- `tmp/` — scratch drafts and prereq prompts
- `.DS_Store` — macOS Finder metadata
- `docs/*.jpg`/draft markdown — works in progress

A bulk-stage sweeps these in and pollutes history. I made this mistake during saga 52 step 002 — `git add -A` swept in tmp/ and .DS_Store. Required a follow-up cleanup commit.

**How to apply:**
- Stage by explicit paths: `git add components/lang-core/ crates/mlpl-array/Cargo.toml ...`
- Use `git add -u` for "stage modifications to already-tracked files" — that's safe; it doesn't add new untracked files
- For mixed additions, list each new file explicitly
- After staging, ALWAYS run `git status --short` and re-check there's nothing you didn't intend

[[agentrail-tracking]]

# Saga 52: components/lang-core/ nested workspace.
#
# Houses the foundational data types that every other component
# depends on:
#   - mlpl-core: spans, identifiers, base types
#   - mlpl-array: DenseArray, Shape (pure compute substrate)
#   - mlpl-eval-core: shared eval types
#
# Pattern matches components/mlpl-session/: a nested workspace
# whose member crates are removed from the main workspace's
# members list. Path deps reach across components via relative
# paths like `../../../<other-component>/crates/<dep>`.
#
# Build cache is shared via `.cargo/config.toml` at the repo root
# (saga 51), so this workspace writes to `sw-mlpl/target/` not
# its own target subdirectory.

[workspace]
members = [
    "crates/mlpl-array",
    "crates/mlpl-core",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
version = "0.20.0"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"

content.text:
You're absolutely right — the whole point. A move is just relocation. The retirement comes from splitting the crowded crate into sparse siblings within the component. mlpl-array has 13 modules (FAIL); leaving it as one crate inside lang-core doesn't retire anything. Splitting it into `mlpl-array-dense` / `mlpl-array-shape` / `mlpl-array-indexing` / `mlpl-array-ops` (each sparse) retires the FAIL and gives the component its purpose.

Let me lock this in and act on it.

input.content:
---
name: move-and-split
description: A component migration is move-and-split — moving without splitting crowded crates leaves the FAILs intact and misses the whole point
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A component migration is **move-AND-split**, not just move.

When you move a crowded crate (one with module-count or fn-count FAILs/WARNs) into a new component, the same saga must also SPLIT it into multiple sparse sibling crates within that component. Otherwise the FAIL persists in the moved crate and the migration achieved nothing structural — just relocation.

**Why:** The whole point of having components is that components hold *sparse* sibling crates. A component containing one 13-module crate is no better than the original flat workspace had — sw-checklist still FAILs on that crate. The retirements come from the split: 1 crate with 13 modules (FAIL) → 4 sibling crates with 3-4 modules each (PASS).

**How to apply:**
- Before each component migration saga, identify which crates inside the target component are crowded (>7 modules, >7 fns/module, or any FAIL)
- The saga's step plan must include `split-<crate>` steps for each crowded crate, not just `move-<crate>` steps
- The close step's sw-checklist delta SHOULD show retired FAILs after a component migration — if it shows zero delta, the migration was incomplete
- Example: lang-core's saga (52) closed with 0 FAILs retired despite moving mlpl-array (13 modules, FAIL). That was wrong — the saga should have included a `split-mlpl-array` step that decomposed it into siblings.

**Concrete crowded crates to split during their migration saga:**
- mlpl-array: 13 modules -> split during lang-core saga (need to revisit saga 52 OR do a follow-up saga)
- mlpl-viz: 13 modules -> split during viz saga
- mlpl-eval: 96 modules -> split into many siblings during eval saga (catastrophic; needs careful sub-planning)
- mlpl-web: 75 modules -> split into many siblings during web saga
- mlpl-serve: 9 modules -> split during serve saga
- mlpl-runtime: 4 modules (PASS), but builtins.rs may still need attention
- mlpl-autograd: 7 modules at the limit + 2 modules with FAIL fn-counts (backward, reduction_ops)

[[components-not-optional]] [[split-aggressively]] [[component-architecture]]

# Decompose mlpl-array into sparse siblings (saga 53)

Saga 52 moved mlpl-array into components/lang-core/ but left its
13 modules intact -- still a Crate Module Count FAIL. The
component migration is incomplete without the SPLIT.

Goal: decompose the 13-module mlpl-array into multiple sparse
sibling crates within components/lang-core/. Use the
extension-trait pattern so all 600+ call sites of `a.matmul(&b)`
etc. keep working with one new `use` line per file.

## Why extension traits

Operations currently live as `impl DenseArray { fn matmul(...) }`.
Splitting these to free functions in another crate breaks every
call site (`a.matmul(&b)` -> `matmul(&a, &b)`).

Extension traits keep the method syntax:
```rust
// In mlpl-array-matmul:
pub trait MatmulExt {
    fn matmul(&self, other: &DenseArray) -> Result<DenseArray, ArrayError>;
}
impl MatmulExt for DenseArray { ... }
pub mod prelude { pub use super::MatmulExt; }

// At call sites (one-line change per file):
use mlpl_array_matmul::prelude::*;
a.matmul(&b)?  // unchanged
```

## Proposed splits

After saga 53, components/lang-core/crates/ contains:
- mlpl-core: spans, identifiers, base types (unchanged)
- mlpl-array: DenseArray + Shape + dense/shape/error/display/indexing
  (5-6 modules, sparse)
- mlpl-array-ops-element: ops_binop, ops_strides as extension trait
- mlpl-array-ops-shape: ops_reshape, ops_transpose
- mlpl-array-ops-reduce: ops_reduce (reduce_axis, argmax_axis)
- mlpl-array-ops-compose: ops_concat (concat, stack, patchify, take)
- mlpl-array-ops-matmul: ops_matmul (matmul, dot)
- mlpl-eval-core (unchanged)

mlpl-array goes from 13 modules (FAIL) to ~6 (PASS).
Each new sibling has 1-2 modules and 1-4 functions (PASS).

Also opportunistically retires Function LOC warnings as we touch
each operation (matmul 50, reduce_axis 46, argmax_axis 44,
patchify 43, stack 43, apply_binop 43, take 41, concat 34,
transpose 37).

## Step plan

1. **scaffold-siblings**: create the 5 new sibling crate skeletons
   (Cargo.toml + lib.rs + prelude) and register in lang-core
   workspace. Verify empty siblings + main + others all build.
2. **split-ops-matmul**: extract ops_matmul.rs into mlpl-array-ops-matmul
   as MatmulExt + DotExt. Update mlpl-array's lib.rs to remove the
   moved file. Find and update all callers (~50 sites likely) to add
   the `use` line. Verify build + tests.
3. **split-ops-reduce**: extract ops_reduce.rs (ReduceExt, ArgmaxExt).
4. **split-ops-compose**: extract ops_concat.rs (ConcatExt, StackExt,
   PatchifyExt, TakeExt).
5. **split-ops-shape**: extract ops_reshape.rs + ops_transpose.rs
   (ReshapeExt, TransposeExt).
6. **split-ops-element**: extract ops_binop.rs + ops_strides.rs.
7. **close**: sw-checklist delta. Expect mlpl-array FAIL retired
   plus 8-10 Function LOC warnings retired.

Each step ends with green cargo check + test from all 4 workspaces
and is committed individually -- if a step fails, the tree is still
on a working revision.

content.text: Saving the regression-test directive and applying it.

input.content:
---
name: test-refactors
description: Every refactor step must run `cargo test` on the affected crates to verify behavior is preserved, not just `cargo check`
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Every refactor step must verify there are no regressions, not just that the code still compiles. `cargo check` proves the type system is happy; `cargo test` proves behavior is preserved.

**Why:** The user has been burned by refactors that "compile clean" but silently broke runtime behavior — golden outputs change, demos misbehave, integration tests fail. A move/split that passes `cargo check` is only halfway done.

**How to apply per refactor step:**
1. `cargo check --workspace` AND each component's `cargo check` from its root — type-level safety
2. `cargo test -p <affected-crate>` for every crate touched — direct unit/integration tests
3. `cargo test -p <downstream-crate>` for at least one or two downstream consumers — catch breakages where the refactor changed an interface
4. For interpreter or eval changes: `cargo test -p mlpl-eval --release` to verify demos still work
5. If any test fails, fix it before committing — don't ship a broken refactor

**Specific places this matters:**

Every refactor step must verify there are no regressions, not just that the code still compiles. `cargo check` proves the type system is happy; `cargo test` proves behavior is preserved.

**Why:** The user has been burned by refactors that "compile clean" but silently broke runtime behavior — golden outputs change, demos misbehave, integration tests fail. A move/split that passes `cargo check` is only halfway done.

**How to apply per refactor step:**
1. `cargo check --workspace` AND each component's `cargo check` from its root — type-level safety
2. `cargo test -p <affected-crate>` for every crate touched — direct unit/integration tests
3. `cargo test -p <downstream-crate>` for at least one or two downstream consumers — catch breakages where the refactor changed an interface
4. For interpreter or eval changes: `cargo test -p mlpl-eval --release` to verify demos still work
5. If any test fails, fix it before committing — don't ship a broken refactor

- Splitting a crate — tests in the original crate that test moved functionality should still work (use dev-deps to import the new sibling)
- Renaming/restructuring — golden-file tests catch what unit tests miss

add_dep() {
  local file=$1
  local rel=$2
  if ! grep -q 'mlpl-array-ops-reduce = ' "$file"; then
    awk -v rel="$rel" '
      /^mlpl-array = / && !done { print; print "mlpl-array-ops-reduce = { path = \"" rel "\" }"; done=1; next }
      { print }
    ' "$file" > "$file.new" && mv "$file.new" "$file"
  fi
}

# mlpl-array gets dev-dep
cat >> components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array/Cargo.toml <<'EOF'
mlpl-array-ops-reduce = { path = "../mlpl-array-ops-reduce" }
EOF

# Consumer crates
add_dep crates/mlpl-eval/Cargo.toml "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array-ops-reduce"
add_dep crates/mlpl-rt/Cargo.toml "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array-ops-reduce"
add_dep crates/mlpl-runtime-array/Cargo.toml "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array-ops-reduce"

# Add use lines to source files
for f in \
  components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array/tests/dense_tests.rs \
  crates/mlpl-eval/src/eval_reduce.rs \
  crates/mlpl-eval/src/model_eval_apply.rs \
  crates/mlpl-rt/src/reductions.rs \
  crates/mlpl-rt/src/transforms.rs \
  crates/mlpl-runtime-array/src/reduce.rs; do
  if ! grep -q "mlpl_array_ops_reduce" "$f"; then
    awk 'BEGIN{i=0} /^use / && !i { print "use mlpl_array_ops_reduce::prelude::*;"; i=1 } { print } END { if(!i) print "use mlpl_array_ops_reduce::prelude::*;" }' "$f" > "$f.new" && mv "$f.new" "$f"
  fi
done
echo "Done."

add_dep() {
  local file=$1
  local rel=$2
  if ! grep -q 'mlpl-array-ops-compose = ' "$file"; then
    awk -v rel="$rel" '
      /^mlpl-array = / && !done { print; print "mlpl-array-ops-compose = { path = \"" rel "\" }"; done=1; next }
      { print }
    ' "$file" > "$file.new" && mv "$file.new" "$file"
  fi
}

# Dev-dep for mlpl-array's own tests
cat >> components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array/Cargo.toml <<'EOF'
mlpl-array-ops-compose = { path = "../mlpl-array-ops-compose" }
EOF

# Consumers
add_dep crates/mlpl-autograd/Cargo.toml "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array-ops-compose"
add_dep crates/mlpl-runtime-array/Cargo.toml "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array-ops-compose"

[package]
name = "mlpl-eval"
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
version.workspace = true

[features]
default = []
# Saga 14 step 004: dispatch ops inside `device("mlx") { }` blocks
# through the `mlpl-mlx-rt` runtime. Off by default; the `mlpl-mlx-rt`
# crate itself triple-gates on macOS + aarch64, so building with
# this feature on a non-Apple host still compiles and falls back
# to CPU at runtime with a one-time warning.
mlx = ["dep:mlpl-mlx-rt", "mlpl-mlx-rt/mlx"]
# Saga 29 step 003: PNG / JPEG decode for the `load_images(dir,
# [H, W])` builtin. Off by default so the WASM target stays
# clean -- the browser REPL can still call
# `load_preloaded("pets_tiny")` because that fixture is
# pre-decoded bytes in the binary. Native binaries
# (`mlpl-cli`, `mlpl-repl`, `mlpl-serve`) enable this feature
# at build time. The decoder dispatch reads the file's magic
# bytes and routes to `png` or `jpeg-decoder` separately

content.text:
## What `vendor/mlx-rs/` is

**`mlx-rs`** is a third-party Rust crate published on crates.io by the **oxideai** organization. It provides Rust bindings for Apple's **MLX** machine-learning framework (the C++/Metal/Accelerate library Apple released in 2023 for its silicon). MLPL uses it indirectly through `mlpl-mlx-rt` (a thin runtime adapter) to dispatch tensor ops to MLX-accelerated kernels when running on Apple hardware.

## Why it's vendored

`mlx-rs` 0.25.3 has an upstream packaging bug: it declares its dependency on `mlx-sys` without `default-features = false`. That accidentally pins on the `metal` feature, which requires the full Xcode.app shader compilers — not the Command Line Tools most Rust devs have. As a result, anyone trying to build mlpl with Apple-acceleration support would fail unless they had Xcode installed.

Project did NOT want to require Xcode. So `vendor/mlx-rs/` is a frozen copy of the crates.io tarball with **one** line added to `Cargo.toml`:

```diff
 [dependencies.mlx-sys]
 version = "=0.2.0"
+default-features = false
```

That's it. Source code, build scripts, `Cargo.lock` are byte-identical to upstream. `Cargo.toml.orig` keeps the original verbatim for reference.

## How Cargo wires it in

Each top-level workspace that transitively depends on `mlx-rs` adds:

```toml
[patch.crates-io]
mlx-rs = { path = "../../vendor/mlx-rs" }
```

Cargo's `[patch]` mechanism replaces the registry copy with the local path during resolution. Anything that does `mlx-rs = "0.25.3"` in its `Cargo.toml` transparently picks up the vendored copy with the fix. No call sites change.

## What this means for refactoring

The vendoring policy is deliberately minimal: **one-line patch, planned removal**. The doc says "when `mlx-rs` publishes a release with the one-line fix (or `mlx-sys` removes `metal` from its defaults), this directory can be deleted and the `[patch.crates-io]` entry dropped."

So even though `vendor/mlx-rs/src/ops/arithmetic.rs` is 2899 lines (the biggest File LOC FAIL in the whole project), it's **not our code to refactor**. Splitting it would:

1. **Diverge our copy from upstream** — making future upgrades a manual merge instead of a `vendor.sh` re-pull.
2. **Inflate the patch surface** — instead of one line, we'd own structural changes to 58 public functions across multiple new files.
3. **Hide the bug fix** — the entire reason for vendoring is the one `default-features = false` line; everything else should be a no-op.
4. **Block the planned removal** — when upstream fixes the packaging bug and we delete `vendor/mlx-rs/`, we'd lose all our split work.

## What I'd recommend instead

The sw-checklist FAILs from `mlx-rs` (32 of them — module fn counts, file LOCs, function LOCs) are **upstream maintenance issues**. We have two clean options:

1. **Exclude vendor/ from sw-checklist** (probably one line of config). Vendor code is by definition not our standard.
2. **Push the fix upstream** — file an issue / PR on github.com/oxideai/mlx-rs with the `default-features = false` change, get it released, then delete `vendor/mlx-rs/` entirely. The FAILs vanish along with our maintenance burden.

For OUR code's >350-line (WARN) files — those are real targets. Let me check what's there if you want me to go after them.

content.text:
You're right — 12 crates in one component is too many. Let me address that immediately. (The editor_panel edit didn't apply due to the Read-first error, so working tree is clean except for the in-progress handlers_submit refactor.)

## Why runtime has 12 crates (the history)

Saga 50 extracted 5 sparse siblings (math, conv, rnn, array, ml) from the original monolithic `mlpl-runtime` to retire FAILs. Saga 55 then bulk-moved everything that was already named `mlpl-runtime-*` into a single `components/runtime/` workspace. The decomposition was right at the **crate** level; the **component** grouping wasn't reconsidered.

## Proposed regrouping into sub-components

Looking at the 12 crates by dependency layer and concern:

```
components/runtime/                  → split into:

components/runtime-core/             (2 crates — dispatch facade + base types)
├── mlpl-runtime           (call_builtin dispatch + try_external chain)
└── mlpl-runtime-core      (RuntimeError, Xorshift64 PRNG)

components/runtime-ops/              (5 crates — element / shape / nn op compute)
├── mlpl-runtime-math      (pi, exp, log, sigmoid, fill, concat, ...)
├── mlpl-runtime-array     (shape, reshape, transpose, reduce, argmax, ...)
├── mlpl-runtime-conv      (conv2d, pool2d)
├── mlpl-runtime-rnn       (rnn_cell, lstm_cell)
└── mlpl-runtime-ml        (softmax, cross_entropy, one_hot, sinusoidal)

components/runtime-data/             (1 crate — data ingest)
└── mlpl-runtime-data      (dataset builtins, embedding builtins, grid)

components/runtime-dr/               (3 crates — dimensionality reduction)
├── mlpl-runtime-dim-reduction  (t-SNE, PCA)
├── mlpl-runtime-umap           (UMAP)
└── mlpl-runtime-mds-rp         (MDS, random projection)

components/ml-helpers/               (1 crate — top-level ML library)
└── mlpl-ml                (high-level ML helpers; depends on runtime)
```

5 sub-components, **each with 1–5 crates**. Each one is a sparse, single-concept grouping.

### Dependency direction (still a DAG)

```
runtime-core ←─── runtime-ops
     ↑              ↑
     ├──── runtime-data
     ├──── runtime-dr
     └──── ml-helpers (also depends on runtime-ops)
```

### Migration cost

Each sub-component gets its own `Cargo.toml` workspace + `[patch.crates-io]` if needed. Inter-component paths update (`../mlpl-runtime-X` → `../../runtime-X/crates/mlpl-runtime-X`). External consumers update too (some apps import `mlpl-runtime`, others import `mlpl-runtime-dim-reduction` directly).

Want me to do this regrouping now? It's structural (no sw-checklist FAIL change directly) but **fixes the "too many crates per component" anti-pattern**. If yes I'll also audit the other components for the same problem before continuing the function-LOC sagas.

**Hard rule: each component workspace has <=4 crates.** sw-checklist warns at >4, fails at >7 — but the sparse target is well under the warning line.

If a feature has more than 4 crates, split into multiple sub-components, e.g.:
- `components/runtime-core/`, `components/runtime-element/`, `components/runtime-layers/`, `components/runtime-data/`, `components/runtime-dr/` instead of one fat `components/runtime/`.

**Why:** The "sparse" principle the user has emphasized throughout: small, focused units at every level (function, module, crate, component). A 12-crate component is no better than a 12-module crate — it shifts the sprawl up a level without fixing it.

- Before creating a new component, plan its expected crate count
- If >4, split into themed sub-components (per concern, layer, or dependency)
- When reviewing existing components, audit crate counts and propose splits

# Sub-component mapping for runtime-X crates
python3 <<'PY'
import re, os

# Map each runtime-* crate to its sub-component
crate_to_sub = {
    'mlpl-runtime': 'runtime-core',
    'mlpl-runtime-core': 'runtime-core',
    'mlpl-runtime-math': 'runtime-element',
    'mlpl-runtime-array': 'runtime-element',
    'mlpl-runtime-conv': 'runtime-layers',
    'mlpl-runtime-rnn': 'runtime-layers',
    'mlpl-runtime-ml': 'runtime-layers',
    'mlpl-runtime-data': 'runtime-data',
    'mlpl-runtime-dim-reduction': 'runtime-dr',
    'mlpl-runtime-umap': 'runtime-dr',
    'mlpl-runtime-mds-rp': 'runtime-dr',
    'mlpl-ml': 'ml-helpers',
}

# Walk every Cargo.toml in components/ and substitute paths
for root, dirs, files in os.walk('components'):
    for f in files:
        if f != 'Cargo.toml':
            continue
        p = os.path.join(root, f)
        with open(p) as fh:
            c = fh.read()
        new = c
        # For each crate, replace the old path patterns with the new sub-component-aware path
        for crate, sub in crate_to_sub.items():
            # Old paths from inside the now-removed components/runtime/ workspace:
            # `path = "../mlpl-runtime-X"` (sibling within runtime/crates)
            # `path = "../../../runtime/crates/mlpl-runtime-X"` (from another component)
            # `path = "../../runtime/crates/mlpl-runtime-X"` (from another workspace at the same level)
            
            # Compute the new path FROM this Cargo.toml's location:
            # this_dir = root, target = components/<sub>/crates/<crate>
            from_path = os.path.relpath(f'components/{sub}/crates/{crate}', start=root)
            
            # Replace any of the old patterns:
            old_patterns = [
                f'path = "../{crate}"',
                f'path = "../../../runtime/crates/{crate}"',
                f'path = "../../runtime/crates/{crate}"',
                f'path = "../../components/runtime/crates/{crate}"',
                f'path = "../../../components/runtime/crates/{crate}"',
            ]
            for old in old_patterns:
                new_str = f'path = "{from_path}"'
                new = new.replace(old, new_str)
        if new != c:
            with open(p, 'w') as fh:
                fh.write(new)
            print(f'Updated {p}')
PY

cd /Users/mike/github/sw-ml-study/sw-mlpl
agentrail archive 2>&1 | tail -1

# Saga 68: split lang-syntax (11 crates)
cat > /tmp/saga68.md <<'EOF'
# Split lang-syntax (11 crates) into sparse sub-components (saga 68)

- syntax-tokens (2):  mlpl-lexer-token, mlpl-lexer-error
- syntax-lex (4):     mlpl-lex-string, mlpl-lex-number, mlpl-lex-punct, mlpl-lex-ident
- syntax-lexer (1):   mlpl-lexer
- syntax-parser (2):  mlpl-parser, mlpl-parser-ast
- syntax-codegen (2): mlpl-macro, mlpl-lower-rs
EOF
agentrail init --name "split-lang-syntax" --plan /tmp/saga68.md 2>&1 | tail -1
agentrail add --slug "split" --prompt "Split" --task-type "refactor"
agentrail add --slug "close" --prompt "Close" --task-type "docs"
agentrail begin 2>&1 | tail -1

# Create sub-components
for sub in syntax-tokens syntax-lex syntax-lexer syntax-parser syntax-codegen; do
  mkdir -p "components/$sub/crates"
  cat > "components/$sub/Cargo.toml" <<EOF
# Saga 68: split out from components/lang-syntax/.

[workspace]
members = []
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
version = "0.20.0"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"
EOF
done

# Move crates
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lexer-token components/syntax-tokens/crates/
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lexer-error components/syntax-tokens/crates/

git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lex-string components/syntax-lex/crates/
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lex-number components/syntax-lex/crates/
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lex-punct components/syntax-lex/crates/
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lex-ident components/syntax-lex/crates/

git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lexer components/syntax-lexer/crates/

git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-parser components/syntax-parser/crates/
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-parser-ast components/syntax-parser/crates/

git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-macro components/syntax-codegen/crates/
git mv components/lang-syntax/crates/mlpl-lower-rs components/syntax-codegen/crates/

rm -rf components/lang-syntax
echo "Done moving."

# Populate members
python3 <<'PY'
populate = {
  'syntax-tokens': ['mlpl-lexer-error', 'mlpl-lexer-token'],
  'syntax-lex': ['mlpl-lex-ident', 'mlpl-lex-number', 'mlpl-lex-punct', 'mlpl-lex-string'],
  'syntax-lexer': ['mlpl-lexer'],
  'syntax-parser': ['mlpl-parser', 'mlpl-parser-ast'],
  'syntax-codegen': ['mlpl-lower-rs', 'mlpl-macro'],
}
for sub, crates in populate.items():
  p = f'components/{sub}/Cargo.toml'
  with open(p) as f: c = f.read()
  members = ',\n    '.join(f'"crates/{cr}"' for cr in crates)
  c = c.replace('members = []', f'members = [\n    {members},\n]')
  with open(p, 'w') as f: f.write(c)
PY

# Build sub-component path map for syntax crates
python3 <<'PY'
import os
crate_to_sub = {
  'mlpl-lexer-token': 'syntax-tokens',
  'mlpl-lexer-error': 'syntax-tokens',
  'mlpl-lex-string': 'syntax-lex',
  'mlpl-lex-number': 'syntax-lex',
  'mlpl-lex-punct': 'syntax-lex',
  'mlpl-lex-ident': 'syntax-lex',
  'mlpl-lexer': 'syntax-lexer',
  'mlpl-parser': 'syntax-parser',
  'mlpl-parser-ast': 'syntax-parser',
  'mlpl-macro': 'syntax-codegen',
  'mlpl-lower-rs': 'syntax-codegen',
}
for root, dirs, files in os.walk('components'):
  for f in files:
    if f != 'Cargo.toml': continue
    p = os.path.join(root, f)
    with open(p) as fh: c = fh.read()
    new = c
    for crate, sub in crate_to_sub.items():
      from_path = os.path.relpath(f'components/{sub}/crates/{crate}', start=root)
      olds = [
        f'path = "../{crate}"',
        f'path = "../../../lang-syntax/crates/{crate}"',
        f'path = "../../lang-syntax/crates/{crate}"',
        f'path = "../../components/lang-syntax/crates/{crate}"',
        f'path = "../../../components/lang-syntax/crates/{crate}"',
        f'path = "../../../../crates/{crate}"',  # very rare
      ]
      for old in olds:
        new = new.replace(old, f'path = "{from_path}"')
    if new != c:
      with open(p, 'w') as fh: fh.write(new)
PY

  echo "$sub: $result"
done

content.text:
## Why these crates exploded to 75–96 modules

### mlpl-eval (96) — the interpreter

A tree-walking interpreter that's doing too many jobs at once. Each prefix is a sub-system that grew under "one-concept-per-file":

| Prefix | Count | What it is |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| `env_*` | **26** | `impl Environment` extensions — one per state category (vars, devices, models, tensors, peers, dirs, params, tokenizers, frozen, tags, records, strings, ...) |
| `model_*` | **18** | The model DSL has ~9 ops × 2 layers (`apply_*` compute + `eval_*` dispatcher) |
| `eval_*` | **11** | Eval dispatcher — one file per AST node category |
| `fetch_*` | 6 | Dataset download/fetch pipeline |
| `inspect_*` | 5 | `:inspect` / `:describe` introspection |
| `grad_*` | 4 | Autograd-tape integration |
| `fncall_*` | 4 | Built-in function call dispatch |
| `error_*` | 4 | Error type + formatting |
| `tag_*`, `image_*`, `experiment_*` | 6 | Smaller subsystems |
| Singletons | 12 | env, error, value, type, device, result, tokenizer, ... |

**The accretion pattern**: each new saga ("add a model op", "add a dataset format", "add another state category") added 1–3 modules. After 50+ sagas, there are 96 modules.

**The structural root cause**: `Environment` is **the kitchen-sink type**. Every operation hangs methods off it via `impl Environment { fn manage_X() }`. By Rust orphan rules, all 26 `env_*.rs` files MUST live in the same crate as `Environment`. They can't move without either:
- splitting `Environment` itself into smaller types
- or refactoring all 26 files into extension traits (like we did for `mlpl-array`'s `ApplyBinopExt`/`MatmulExt`/etc.)

### mlpl-web (75) — the frontend

The entire Yew app + every demo + every learning path + every UI component bundled together:

| Prefix | Count | What it is |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| `demos_*` | **12** | One file per demo (lin reg, MLP, CNN, GAN, autoencoder, transformer, ...) — accreted over capability sagas |
| `render_*` | **11** | Render branches (header, main shell, history, completion popup, glossary, ...) |
| `paths_*` | 6 | Learning path content (Pixels-to-Language, History, Optimizers, etc.) |
| `component_*` | 6 | Yew components (mode bar, doc dialog, splash, ...) |
| `app_*` | 6 | Top-level app wiring + state |
| `handlers_*` | 5 | Event handlers (submit, click, viz3d, etc.) |
| `onboarding_*` | 4 | Splash + tour + what's-new |
| `viz3d_*`, `mode_*`, `upload_*`, `glossary_*` | 10 | Feature clusters |
| Singletons | 15 | lib, entry, editor, completion, ... |

**The accretion pattern**: every "content" saga added a demo and/or a learning path; every "feature" saga added handlers + components. Without sub-component boundaries, it all piled into one crate.

**The structural root cause**: `AppState` (and its hooks) is **the kitchen-sink state**. Same problem as `Environment` — every handler/render branch takes `AppState` references. Splitting requires either extension-trait pattern or splitting AppState.

## Why the 5±2 guideline doesn't help directly

The 5±2 rule is about **cognitive complexity at one zoom level**. A 96-module crate isn't a 96-concept abstraction — it's a 10-concept feature area where each concept got `N` files. The right intervention is **structural decomposition at the component/crate level**, not file consolidation. If I tried to merge `env_*.rs` files to get under 7 modules, each merged file would be 1000+ lines (FAIL on a different axis).

3. **Extract `experiment_*` + `inspect_*`** — moderate Environment use; lift to extension traits.
4. **Hard part: refactor `Environment` itself.** Break the 26 env_*.rs `impl Environment` blocks into extension traits. Each `EnvFooExt` lives in its own sibling crate. Environment itself shrinks to a thin struct. This is the same pattern that worked for `mlpl-array`'s 13-module problem.
5. **Decompose `model_*`** — once `Environment` is extension-trait-ified, the 18 model files can move to siblings.

This is multi-saga work. The first three are mechanical; #4 is the architectural lift. After those, eval drops from 96 → maybe 15 across 5–7 sibling crates in a single `components/eval-X/` family.

**For mlpl-web:**

1. **Extract `demos_*` into `components/web-demos/`** — pure content, takes minimal state.
2. **Extract `paths_*` into `components/web-content/`** — same.
3. **Extract `onboarding_*` into `components/web-onboarding/`** — splash/tour/what's-new are self-contained.
4. **Extract `viz3d_*` into `components/web-viz3d/`** — 3D scene management.
5. **Hard part: `AppState` decomposition** — similar to Environment.

# Build pages/ for GitHub Pages deployment.
# Run this before committing pages/ changes.

input.content:
# Decomposing the god crates (mlpl-eval, mlpl-web)

This doc captures the strategy for fixing the two largest module-count
FAILs in the codebase: `mlpl-eval` (96 modules) and `mlpl-web` (75
modules). Both are "god crates" — single workspace members that
centralize an entire feature area instead of spreading its concerns
across multiple sibling crates.

## Why they grew so big

### mlpl-eval (96 modules, by prefix)

| Prefix | Count | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `env_*` | 26 | `impl Environment` extensions, one per state category |
| `model_*` | 18 | Model DSL: ~9 ops x 2 layers (`apply_*` + `eval_*`) |
| `eval_*` | 11 | Eval dispatcher per AST node category |
| `fetch_*` | 6 | Dataset download / fetch pipeline |
| `inspect_*` | 5 | `:inspect` / `:describe` introspection |
| `grad_*` | 4 | Autograd-tape integration |
| `fncall_*` | 4 | Built-in function call dispatch |
| `error_*` | 4 | Error type + formatting |
| `tag_*`, `image_*`, `experiment_*` | 6 | Smaller subsystems |
| Singletons | 12 | value, type, device, result, tokenizer, ... |

**Root cause:** `Environment` is the kitchen-sink type. Every operation
hangs methods off it via `impl Environment { fn manage_X() }`. By
Rust's orphan rule, all 26 `env_*.rs` files MUST live in the same
crate as `Environment`. They can't move out without either:

1. Splitting `Environment` itself into smaller types, OR
2. Refactoring all 26 files into extension traits (`EnvFooExt`).

### mlpl-web (75 modules, by prefix)

| Prefix | Count | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `demos_*` | 12 | One file per demo (lin reg, MLP, CNN, GAN, ...) |
| `render_*` | 11 | Render branches (header, main, history, completion, ...) |
| `paths_*` | 6 | Learning path content (one file per path) |
| `component_*`, `components.rs` | 7 | Yew components |
| `app_*` | 6 | Top-level app wiring + state |
| `handlers_*` | 5 | Event handlers |
| `onboarding_*` | 4 | Splash + tour + what's-new |
| `viz3d_*`, `mode_*`, `upload_*`, `glossary_*` | 10 | Feature clusters |
| Singletons | 14 | lib, entry, editor, completion, ... |

**Root cause:** `AppState` is the kitchen-sink state, same problem as
`Environment`. Every handler and render branch takes `AppState`
references. Splitting requires either extension-trait pattern or
`AppState` decomposition.

## Why the 5+/-2 guideline doesn't apply directly

The 5+/-2 rule is about cognitive complexity at one zoom level. A
96-module crate isn't a 96-concept abstraction -- it's a 10-concept
feature area where each concept got N files. The right intervention is
structural decomposition at the component/crate level, not file
consolidation. Merging `env_*.rs` files to get under 7 modules would
produce 1000+ line files (FAIL on a different axis).

## Decomposition strategy

The pattern that worked for `mlpl-array` (saga 53): extract operation
families into sibling extension-trait crates within a sub-component,
preserving call-site syntax via `prelude` modules.

### Phase 1: mechanical extractions (no Environment/AppState refactor)

These groups have minimal or no dependency on the kitchen-sink type
and can move out today:

**mlpl-eval:**
- `image_*` (2 files, 0 Environment refs) -> `components/eval-image/`
- `fetch_*` (6 files, 1 Environment ref) -> `components/eval-fetch/`
- `experiment_*` (2 files, 1 ref) -> `components/eval-experiment/`
- `inspect_*` (5 files, 3 refs) -> `components/eval-inspect/` (some
  inspect functions need Environment access; lift to extension trait
  or pass smaller types)

Drops mlpl-eval from 96 to ~80 modules. Still FAIL but big reduction.

**mlpl-web:**
- `demos_*` (12) -> `components/web-demos/`
- `paths_*` (6) -> `components/web-paths/`
- `onboarding_*` (4) -> `components/web-onboarding/`
- `viz3d_*` (3) -> `components/web-viz3d/`

Drops mlpl-web from 75 to ~50 modules. Still FAIL but big reduction.

### Phase 2: trait inversion (the hard lift)

Both `Environment` and `AppState` need to shrink. The fix is the same
pattern that worked for `DenseArray`:

1. Identify which fields/methods truly belong on the core type vs
   which are sub-systems hung off it.
2. For each sub-system, define an extension trait + impl in a sibling
   crate:
   ```rust
   // In mlpl-eval-env-vars (sibling crate):
   pub trait EnvVarsExt {
       fn get_var(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Value>;
       fn set_var(&mut self, name: String, value: Value);
   }
   impl EnvVarsExt for Environment { ... }
   pub mod prelude { pub use super::EnvVarsExt; }
   ```
3. Callers pick up `use mlpl_eval_env_vars::prelude::*;` -- the
   `env.get_var(...)` call syntax is unchanged.
4. Each extension-trait crate has 1-3 modules of its own. Sparse.

Goal after Phase 2: split mlpl-eval's `env_*` 26 files into ~6 sibling
crates inside `components/eval-env-X/` sub-components, each with 3-5
files.

### Phase 3: model_* and similar dispatch chains

`model_*` (18 files) and `eval_*` (11 files) are dispatch chains where
each file calls others. After Phase 2 lifts `Environment` to a smaller
core, these can move out as sibling crates that take `&mut dyn EnvX`
through the new traits.

## Sub-component grouping (post-decomposition)

After all phases, `mlpl-eval`'s 96 modules become:

```
components/eval-types/        (3)  value, error, env (the core types)
components/eval-image/        (1)  mlpl-eval-image
components/eval-fetch/        (1)  mlpl-eval-fetch
components/eval-experiment/   (1)  mlpl-eval-experiment
components/eval-inspect/      (1)  mlpl-eval-inspect

components/eval-env-vars/     (1)  EnvVarsExt
components/eval-env-models/   (1)  EnvModelsExt
components/eval-env-tensors/  (1)  EnvTensorsExt
components/eval-env-devices/  (1)  EnvDevicesExt
components/eval-env-strings/  (1)  EnvStringsExt
components/eval-env-misc/     (1)  EnvDirsExt, EnvParamsExt, etc.

components/eval-model-apply/  (3)  model_apply, model_apply_*
components/eval-model-eval/   (3)  model_eval_*, model_dispatch
components/eval-model-lora/   (1)  model_lora, model_mutate
components/eval-model-inspect/(1)  model_freeze, model_feasibility

components/eval-dispatch/     (3)  eval_*, fncall_*
components/eval-grad/         (1)  grad_*
components/eval-tag/          (1)  tag_propagate, auto_tag
components/eval/              (1)  facade re-exporting everything
```

That's ~18 sibling crates across ~12 sub-components, each sparse.

For `mlpl-web` similarly:

```
components/web-content/       (3)  demos, paths, glossary
components/web-onboarding/    (1)  splash + tour + what's-new
components/web-viz3d/         (1)  3D scene + handlers
components/web-render/        (3)  render_* split by area
components/web-components/    (3)  Yew components split by concern
components/web-handlers/      (2)  event handlers
components/web-state/         (2)  AppState decomposed
components/web/               (1)  app entry + lib facade
```

# Decomposing the god crates (mlpl-eval, mlpl-web)

This doc captures the strategy for fixing the two largest module-count
FAILs in the codebase: `mlpl-eval` (96 modules) and `mlpl-web` (75
modules). Both are "god crates" — single workspace members that
centralize an entire feature area instead of spreading its concerns
across multiple sibling crates.

## Why they grew so big

### mlpl-eval (96 modules, by prefix)

| Prefix | Count | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `env_*` | 26 | `impl Environment` extensions, one per state category |
| `model_*` | 18 | Model DSL: ~9 ops x 2 layers (`apply_*` + `eval_*`) |
| `eval_*` | 11 | Eval dispatcher per AST node category |
| `fetch_*` | 6 | Dataset download / fetch pipeline |
| `inspect_*` | 5 | `:inspect` / `:describe` introspection |
| `grad_*` | 4 | Autograd-tape integration |
| `fncall_*` | 4 | Built-in function call dispatch |
| `error_*` | 4 | Error type + formatting |
| `tag_*`, `image_*`, `experiment_*` | 6 | Smaller subsystems |
| Singletons | 12 | value, type, device, result, tokenizer, ... |

**Root cause:** `Environment` is the kitchen-sink type. Every operation
hangs methods off it via `impl Environment { fn manage_X() }`. By
Rust's orphan rule, all 26 `env_*.rs` files MUST live in the same
crate as `Environment`. They can't move out without either:

1. Splitting `Environment` itself into smaller types, OR
2. Refactoring all 26 files into extension traits (`EnvFooExt`).

### mlpl-web (75 modules, by prefix)

| Prefix | Count | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `demos_*` | 12 | One file per demo (lin reg, MLP, CNN, GAN, ...) |
| `render_*` | 11 | Render branches (header, main, history, completion, ...) |
| `paths_*` | 6 | Learning path content (one file per path) |
| `component_*`, `components.rs` | 7 | Yew components |
| `app_*` | 6 | Top-level app wiring + state |
| `handlers_*` | 5 | Event handlers |
| `onboarding_*` | 4 | Splash + tour + what's-new |
| `viz3d_*`, `mode_*`, `upload_*`, `glossary_*` | 10 | Feature clusters |
| Singletons | 14 | lib, entry, editor, completion, ... |

**Root cause:** `AppState` is the kitchen-sink state, same problem as
`Environment`. Every handler and render branch takes `AppState`
references. Splitting requires either extension-trait pattern or
`AppState` decomposition.

## Why the 5+/-2 guideline doesn't apply directly

The 5+/-2 rule is about cognitive complexity at one zoom level. A
96-module crate isn't a 96-concept abstraction -- it's a 10-concept
feature area where each concept got N files. The right intervention is
structural decomposition at the component/crate level, not file
consolidation. Merging `env_*.rs` files to get under 7 modules would
produce 1000+ line files (FAIL on a different axis).

## Decomposition strategy

The pattern that worked for `mlpl-array` (saga 53): extract operation
families into sibling extension-trait crates within a sub-component,
preserving call-site syntax via `prelude` modules.

### Phase 1: mechanical extractions (no Environment/AppState refactor)

These groups have minimal or no dependency on the kitchen-sink type
and can move out today:

**mlpl-eval:**
- `image_*` (2 files, 0 Environment refs) -> `components/eval-image/`
- `fetch_*` (6 files, 1 Environment ref) -> `components/eval-fetch/`
- `experiment_*` (2 files, 1 ref) -> `components/eval-experiment/`
- `inspect_*` (5 files, 3 refs) -> `components/eval-inspect/` (some
  inspect functions need Environment access; lift to extension trait
  or pass smaller types)

Drops mlpl-eval from 96 to ~80 modules. Still FAIL but big reduction.

**mlpl-web:**
- `demos_*` (12) -> `components/web-demos/`
- `paths_*` (6) -> `components/web-paths/`
- `onboarding_*` (4) -> `components/web-onboarding/`
- `viz3d_*` (3) -> `components/web-viz3d/`

Drops mlpl-web from 75 to ~50 modules. Still FAIL but big reduction.

### Phase 2: trait inversion (the hard lift)

Both `Environment` and `AppState` need to shrink. The fix is the same
pattern that worked for `DenseArray`:

1. Identify which fields/methods truly belong on the core type vs
   which are sub-systems hung off it.
2. For each sub-system, define an extension trait + impl in a sibling
   crate:
   ```rust
   // In mlpl-eval-env-vars (sibling crate):
   pub trait EnvVarsExt {
       fn get_var(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Value>;
       fn set_var(&mut self, name: String, value: Value);
   }
   impl EnvVarsExt for Environment { ... }
   pub mod prelude { pub use super::EnvVarsExt; }
   ```
3. Callers pick up `use mlpl_eval_env_vars::prelude::*;` -- the
   `env.get_var(...)` call syntax is unchanged.
4. Each extension-trait crate has 1-3 modules of its own. Sparse.

Goal after Phase 2: split mlpl-eval's `env_*` 26 files into ~6 sibling
crates inside `components/eval-env-X/` sub-components, each with 3-5
files.

### Phase 3: model_* and similar dispatch chains

`model_*` (18 files) and `eval_*` (11 files) are dispatch chains where
each file calls others. After Phase 2 lifts `Environment` to a smaller
core, these can move out as sibling crates that take `&mut dyn EnvX`
through the new traits.

## Sub-component grouping (post-decomposition)

After all phases, `mlpl-eval`'s 96 modules become:

```
components/eval-types/        (3)  value, error, env (the core types)
components/eval-image/        (1)  mlpl-eval-image
components/eval-fetch/        (1)  mlpl-eval-fetch
components/eval-experiment/   (1)  mlpl-eval-experiment
components/eval-inspect/      (1)  mlpl-eval-inspect

components/eval-env-vars/     (1)  EnvVarsExt
components/eval-env-models/   (1)  EnvModelsExt
components/eval-env-tensors/  (1)  EnvTensorsExt
components/eval-env-devices/  (1)  EnvDevicesExt
components/eval-env-strings/  (1)  EnvStringsExt
components/eval-env-misc/     (1)  EnvDirsExt, EnvParamsExt, etc.

components/eval-model-apply/  (3)  model_apply, model_apply_*
components/eval-model-eval/   (3)  model_eval_*, model_dispatch
components/eval-model-lora/   (1)  model_lora, model_mutate
components/eval-model-inspect/(1)  model_freeze, model_feasibility

components/eval-dispatch/     (3)  eval_*, fncall_*
components/eval-grad/         (1)  grad_*
components/eval-tag/          (1)  tag_propagate, auto_tag
components/eval/              (1)  facade re-exporting everything
```

That's ~18 sibling crates across ~12 sub-components, each sparse.

For `mlpl-web` similarly:

```
components/web-content/       (3)  demos, paths, glossary
components/web-onboarding/    (1)  splash + tour + what's-new
components/web-viz3d/         (1)  3D scene + handlers
components/web-render/        (3)  render_* split by area
components/web-components/    (3)  Yew components split by concern
components/web-handlers/      (2)  event handlers
components/web-state/         (2)  AppState decomposed
components/web/               (1)  app entry + lib facade
```

## Migration plan (when ready)

1. **One saga per Phase-1 extraction.** Each is mechanical (~30 min)
   and drops 2-12 modules. Total: ~8 sagas, drops eval to ~80 and
   web to ~50.
2. **One saga per Environment / AppState sub-system trait inversion.**
   Each is bigger (~1-2 hours) but high payoff. Total: ~6 sagas, drops
   eval to ~25 modules across the env-X siblings.
3. **One saga per model_* / eval_* dispatch chain.** Total: ~4 sagas.
4. **Mirror approach for mlpl-web.** Total: ~6 sagas.

Estimated 24 sagas total to fully decompose both god crates. Each
ends with `cargo test` green and the sw-checklist count moving in the
right direction.

## Why not just refactor in place

A few alternatives considered and rejected:

- **Merge files to fewer modules.** Trades module-count FAIL for
  file-LOC FAIL. Worse from a code-review perspective.
- **Suppress sw-checklist for these crates.** Defeats the purpose;
  the project standard is uniform.
- **Move everything into a "god component" with many crates.** Just
  shifts the sprawl up a level (see also `feedback_4_per_workspace`
  in memory).

The extension-trait pattern is the only path that preserves call-site
syntax, retires the FAILs, and keeps modules sparse at every zoom
level.

## Status

- Phase 0 (the bottom-up component migration) is **complete** as of

content.text:
Saga 71 closed. **Pattern proven for Phase 1 god-crate decomposition.**

## What landed

**mlpl-eval-image extracted as the first Phase 1 demo:**
- 2 files moved: `image_io.rs` → `io.rs`, `image_io_pixels.rs` → `pixels.rs`
- New component `components/eval-image/` (1 crate, sparse)
- `ImageError(pub String)` newtype avoids the EvalError type-cycle
- `impl From<ImageError> for EvalError` in `error_from_tools.rs` (feature-gated)
- 3 call sites updated to `mlpl_eval_image::*`

**sw-checklist (ours-only):**
| | Pass | FAIL | WARN |
|---|------|------|------|
| Before saga 71 | 296 | 21 | 281 |
| After | 316 | 20 | 284 |
| Delta | **+20** | **-1** | +3 |

mlpl-eval: **96 → 94 modules.** Still FAIL but a clean step down. The pattern is proven: introduce a local error type, bridge with `From`, keep the dependency a clean DAG.

## Pattern recap (for the next 7 Phase 1 sagas)

```
1. New component components/eval-X/, new crate mlpl-eval-X
2. git mv N files into it (rename as needed)
3. Define local ErrorX(pub String) (or richer if needed)
4. Update moved code: EvalError::Variant → ErrorX::new
5. Add `impl From<ErrorX> for EvalError` in mlpl-eval (gated)
6. Update consumers: crate::X:: → mlpl_eval_x::
7. Update mlpl-eval lib.rs: remove old mods, optionally re-export
8. Build all 29 workspaces, test
9. Commit + close
```

**Next candidates (in order of cleanliness):**
- `experiment_*` (2 files, 1 Environment ref) — easy
- `fetch_*` (6 files) — bigger, similar simple error pattern
- `inspect_*` (5 files, 3 Environment refs) — needs care around Environment
- `grad_*` (4 files, 3 Environment refs) — same
- `model_apply_*` subset (the pure-compute ones)
- `error_*` (4 files) — would unlock cleaner extraction of other groups

Want me to do `experiment_*` next? Same recipe, even smaller.
